title: Multicolor Fluorescence Detection for Droplet Microfluidics Using Optical Fibers
protocol: Design microfluidic structures for three-layer fabrication using design software.
Have the designs printed by a vendor on circuit board film with 10 μm resolution.
Place a pre-cleaned 3 inch diameter silicon wafer on a spin coater and turn on the vacuum to affix it to the chuck.
Apply 1 ml of SU8-3050 in the center of the wafer and spin for 20 sec at 500 rpm, then 30 sec at 1,750 rpm.
Bake the coated wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 30 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature before moving on to the next step.
Expose the coated wafer to the 1st layer mask under a collimated 190 mW, 365 nm LED for 3 min.
Place the exposed wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature before proceeding to the next step.
Apply 1 ml of SU8-3050 in the center of the wafer and spin for 20 sec at 500 rpm, then 30 sec at 5,000 rpm.
Remove the wafer and bake on a 135 °C hotplate for 30 min.
Cool to RT after baking.
Align the 2nd layer mask onto the geometry patterned in step 1.3.
Expose the coated wafer to a collimated 190 mW, 365 nm LED for 3 min.
Place the exposed wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 4 min 30 sec after exposure.
Cool to RT after baking.
Place the wafer on the spin coater and turn on the vacuum to affix it to the chuck.
Apply 1 ml of SU8-3050 in the center of the wafer.
Spin at 500 rpm for 20 sec, then at 1,000 rpm for 30 sec.
Remove the wafer after spinning and bake on a 135 °C hotplate for 30 min.
Cool to RT after baking.
Align the 3rd layer mask onto the geometry patterned in step 1.3.
Expose the coated wafer to a collimated 190 mW, 365 nm LED for 3 min.
Place the exposed wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 9 min after exposure.
Cool to RT after baking.
Immersed in a stirred bath of propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate for 30 min to develop masks.
Wash the wafer in isopropanol.
Bake the developed master on a 135 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Place the developed master in a 100 mm Petri dish for PDMS molding.
Combine 50 g of silicone base with 5 g of curing agent in a plastic cup.
Mix the contents with a rotary tool fitted with a stir stick.
Degas the mixture inside a desiccator for 30 min, or until all air bubbles are removed.
Pour the PDMS to give a thickness of 3 mm over the master and place back into the desiccator for further degassing.
Bake the device at 80 °C for 80 min.
Cut the device from the mold using a scalpel.
Place the patterned side up on a clean surface with the patterned side up.
Punch the fluidic inlets and outlets with a 0.75 mm biopsy punch.
Plasma treat the device, with feature side up, along with a pre-cleaned 2 inches by 3 inches glass slide at 1 mbar O2 plasma for 20 sec in a 300 W plasma cleaner.
Place the patterned side of the PDMS device onto the plasma-treated side of the glass slide.
Bake the assembled device at 80 °C for 40 min.
Flush the device with a fluorinated surface treatment fluid using a syringe.
Bake the device at 80 °C for 10 min to evaporate the solvent.
Prepare the 2nd color laser excitation fiber by repeating the steps for a 2nd identical fiber.
Repeat the steps for preparing a fiber for collecting fluorescence signal using a 200 µm core, 225 µm cladding, NA = 0.39 optical fiber.
Inspect the tips of all fibers and re-cleave the ends with a fiber scribe if they do not end in a flat surface.
Attach a laser fiber coupler to a 50 mW, 405 nm laser and attach one of the 105 µm core fibers to the laser.
Direct the stripped end at the sensor of the laser power meter and use fine adjustments to maximize laser power.
Repeat for a 50 mW, 473 nm laser.
Mount a 446/510/581/703 nm quad bandpass filters on the PMT using lens tubes to block laser light and transmit emitted fluorescence.
Attach fiber coupler so that light travels through the filters before hitting the PMT.
Attach the fiber from step 3.3 to the unit assembled in step 3.7.
Obtain a flow focus microfluidics dropmaker device with a 60 µm x 60 µm orifice.
Fill a 1 ml syringe with HFE 7500 oils with 2% ionic fluorosurfactant.
Prepare a series of 1 ml syringes with fluorescein (FITC) and dextran-conjugated blue dyes (CB) in PBS: 1 nM FITC/10 nM CB, 10 nM FITC/10 nM CB, 1 nM FITC/100 nM CB, and 10 nM FITC/100 nM CB.
Mount the dropmaker device on an inverted microscope stage and syringe pumps for aqueous and oil syringes.
Couple syringes to devices using PE-2 tubing.
Run syringe pumps at 500 μl/hr for oil and 250 μl/hr for aqueous solutions to create droplets containing the prepared solutions.
Use a fresh dropmaker device for each type of aqueous sample to avoid cross-contamination.
Collect approximately 200 μl of emulsion from each dye combination into an empty syringe.
Mix the collected emulsion by repeatedly rotating the syringe.
Repeat steps involving the preparation and mixing of droplets with different concentrations of FITC in PBS solutions.
Place the microfluidic chip on the stage of an inverted microscope coupled to a digital camera capable of < 100 μsec shutter speeds.
Insert the fiber coupled to the 473 nm laser into the farthest upstream 120 µm channel, avoiding puncturing through to the main flow channel.
Insert the fiber coupled to the 405 nm laser into the farthest downstream 120 µm high side channel, maintaining a spacing of 300 µm from the first fiber.
Insert the PMT-coupled fiber into the 220 µm tall channel, perpendicular to the two laser excitation fibers.
Mount a 5 ml syringe filled with HFE 7500 containing 2% ionic fluorosurfactant to the spacer oil inlet of the detection device using PE-2 tubing.
Mount the syringe containing the mixed FITC/CB emulsion on a vertically oriented syringe pump.
Couple the syringe to the device's droplet reinjection inlet using PE-2 tubing.
Connect a length of PE-2 tubing from the device exit to a waste container.
Prime the device by running each of the pumps at 1,000 µl/hr until both oil and droplets are seen regularly combining in the device and flowing downstream.
Adjust the flow rates such that the spacer oil runs at 6,000 µl/hr and the droplets at 100 µl/hr.
Turn on the lasers.
Start the data acquisition program.
Adjust the PMT gain to provide signals more than 100x the baseline noise floor.
Adjust the laser power so that all of the doublet peaks are clearly visible on a single, linearly scaled timetrace.
Acquire 60 seconds of the PMT voltage timetrace at at least 20 kHz.
